artists.biography: Soul Asylum is an American alternative rock band that formed in Minneapolis, Minnesota in 1983. The band originally formed in 1981 under the name Loud Fast Rules, with the original line-up consisting of Dan Murphy, Dave Pirner, Karl Mueller and Pat Morley. The latter was replaced by Grant Young in 1984. The band recorded three albums with Twin/Tone Records and two with A&M Records to little commercial success. However, in 1992, they released the triple-platinum album Grave Dancers Union, featuring their Grammy Award-winning single "Runaway Train". The band played the Bill Clinton inauguration early the next year. They also scored a platinum record with the album Let Your Dim Light Shine three years later. In 1998 they recorded Candy from a Stranger. Mueller was diagnosed with cancer in 2004, causing the band to organize a benefit concert on his behalf. Mueller died a year later. In 2006 they released The Silver Lining. Their most recent effort is entitled Delayed Reaction, which was released on July 17, 2012.

perplexity.description:
Grave Dancers Union is the sixth studio album by Minneapolis alternative rock band Soul Asylum, released on October 6, 1992, on Columbia Records. The album marked a significant turning point for the band, arriving after they had struggled to gain commercial traction through independent releases and two albums on the A&M label. In the early 1990s, Soul Asylum repositioned themselves as an unplugged, acoustic act, a shift that caught Columbia Records' attention and led to this major-label debut. The album represents the band's evolution from their early punk roots toward a more melodic alternative rock sound, incorporating diverse musical elements while maintaining the songwriting sensibility they had developed through years of relentless touring.

The album achieved substantial commercial success, becoming Soul Asylum's best-selling release by a considerable margin. It was certified triple-platinum within a year of its release and spent 76 weeks on the Billboard charts. This success was largely driven by the hit single "Runaway Train," which eschewed the fuzzy guitars and obscured vocals typical of grunge in favor of clear, emotional vocals and a direct lyrical plea. The song's accompanying music video, which featured missing children, led to the recovery of 21 of the 36 featured missing kids according to Rolling Stone, and the band's profile was further elevated when they performed at President Bill Clinton's 1993 inauguration.

Musically, Grave Dancers Union showcases the band's melodic strengths across its tracklist, culminating in the acoustic ballad "The Sun Maid," which features orchestral strings and demonstrates the full scope of their songwriting talent. While Soul Asylum would continue releasing albums with moderate acclaim and sales in subsequent decades, Grave Dancers Union remains their commercial and cultural peak, establishing them as significant figures in the early 1990s alternative rock landscape, even as contemporaries like Nirvana came to dominate the era's historical narrative.
